chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mismaʿī and another man, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Do not enter the grave while wearing sandals, nor a cap, nor a cloak, nor a turban." I said: "What about the khuff?" He said: "There is no harm in the khuff, for in removing the khuff there is disgracefulness."

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: a leather sock or boot-like footwear
key_terms.الْقَبْرَ: the grave into which one enters during burial
key_terms.شَنَاعَةً: something unseemly, disgraceful, or awkward in appearance

ai.seo_question: What should a person avoid wearing when entering the grave during burial according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the etiquette of entering the grave during burial. It prohibits entering the grave wearing certain visible garments, while making an exception for the khuff because removing it would involve an unseemly exposure or awkwardness.
